title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations

description.narrative: Uganda faces significant challenges in addressing child labour and promoting decent work in sectors such as coffee, which is critical to the national economy. Approximately 7.9 million children in Uganda are engaged in hazardous work, driven by poverty and limited access to education. In the coffee sector, gaps in core labour standards, including child labour, forced labour, and occupational safety and health (OSH), hinder the realization of fundamental rights at work. The ILO collaborates with Uganda’s workers’ organizations—the National Organization of Trade Unions (NOTU) and the Confederation of Free Trade Unions (COFTU)—to strengthen their capacity to combat child labour and improve working conditions. The initiative supports the integration of child labour and OSH clauses into collective agreements and enhances the ability of workers' organizations to advocate for the application of international labour standards. Key activities include training on negotiation skills, social dialogue, and collective bargaining to address the root causes of child labour. Workers’ organizations are also supported to develop advocacy strategies targeting the reduction of child labour and improved OSH in the coffee sector. Additionally, the intervention promotes greater inclusion of marginalized groups and emphasizes gender equality and disability inclusion. This intervention aligns with Sustainable Development Goals 1, 8, and 15, focusing on poverty eradication, labour rights protection, and sustainable resource use. By fostering collaboration among stakeholders, strengthening institutional capacity, and raising awareness, the initiative seeks to reduce child labour, improve workplace safety, and enhance social protection in Uganda's coffee and related sectors.
